builds.howItPlays: You put cheap Mechs on the board early, and Rumble's ability gives each one +1 Might while it defends, so they're hard to push off a battlefield you hold. Later, Ferrous Forerunner (6 cost) leaves two 3 Might Mech tokens in your base when it dies, and Thousand-Tailed Watcher (7 cost) gives every enemy unit -3 Might on the turn it arrives, so your side wins the big fight.
builds.whyYou: You like a deck with a clear plan: put units down, hold your ground, and let the board grow every turn. There are a few choices along the way, like which Mech to send to the other battlefield or when to save a cheap spell for your opponent's turn, but nothing you have to set up over many turns. You don't mind a game that runs into the middle turns, because your expensive units arrive in time to finish it. If a wide, sturdy board that's hard to clear sounds fun, Rumble suits you.
builds.ratingNotes:
Change 2026-09-25: coordinates move from 4.5/6/4/3 to 5/6/5/4.5. Variance moved 1.5, which triggers the move. Complexity went up 1 and Pace up 0.5. The old rating read the starter deck and a starter-deck guide. It is now the mean of three current tournament and community lists. The deckListUrl was the bare /decks page and is now the display deck. The riftboundguide starter-deck page and hextechanalytics are dropped from guideUrls, because the first describes the starter product and I did not fetch the second on this pass. The label stays Midrange (tools.ts style: Midrange 5/6/5/4.5, mean of 3, labels Midrange x3).

Scored decks: Best of Singapore, PiwisRAwesome, 2026 RQ, https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/62bb68f3-8705-4ffd-8589-d9f3600bf295: 5/5.5/5.5/5. Best of Barcelona, ZNT Agazapado, 2026 RQ, https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/fe139c7f-3222-4a5b-9963-260468ba0764: 5/6/5/4. Rumble - Mech Tribal (VEN), noxiangrandgeneral, https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/89de1489-ad07-4533-aa04-8bdabca9b1e9: 5/6/5/4. None of the three sheets has adjustments, and no Axis had a formula-judgment gap of 2 or more.

Deciding cards. Pace: 8 cheap Mechs (Gem Jammer, Forecaster, Patched Porobot) against 9-10 cards costing 5+ (Ferrous Forerunner, Thousand-Tailed Watcher, Singularity, Breakneck Mech). Stance: 14-18 bodies of pressure against about 9-10 answers (Falling Star, Singularity, Stupefy, Cloth Armor, Brynhir Thundersong). Complexity: moving and readying with Gem Jammer and Bubble Bot, the Hidden Temporal Breach and Consult the Past, and Reaction Stupefy. Variance: no luck or swing cards. Singapore runs mostly 1-2-ofs (30% 3-ofs), which puts it at 5. Barcelona and VEN run 60% 3-ofs, which puts them at 4.

Legend: your Mechs have Shield (+1 Might while they're defenders). It rewards a wide board of Mechs holding battlefields.

Also played: Mech-Jhin, https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/0c074682-726d-4fa6-a28f-7cdf73cb8469 (5/6/6/5: Jhin made a Mech with Experimental Hexplate and equipped with Blighted Battleaxe). Danger Zone Mech Swarm, https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/3090cf9b-508b-4b9a-8fa1-6d18d54ffad9 (5.5/6/5.5/4), https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/ff34802c-4225-4da9-8c25-2cd773901e79 (5.5/6/5.5/4.5) and https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/75cc627d-fed1-4aa9-900f-123344a8f75a (5/6/6/4.5): these go wide with Iterative Design and Production Surge tokens pumped by Danger Zone. The merged Eclipse / Deadly Flourish control lists (Utrecht RQ Best of, 39 cards, unscored) and the Rage Amplifier / Wages of Pain lists also play this Build.

Confidence: low.

Reviewer check: the Barcelona (fe139c7f) and VEN (89de1489) sheets have identical scorer inputs, so they may be the same 40 cards. If they are, the mean effectively double-counts one list, though Singapore alone would still give about 5/5.5/5.5/5. The display deck is the Arcane Academy copy of the Singapore Best of, because the system post (505bf400) has only 39 cards.
